Tosafot on Bava Batra 52b:10:1.hebrew: נעל וגדר כל שהוא כו' - בגמרא פר"ש דהאי נעל היינו שקבע מנעול בדלת דהוי בנין, אבל סגר הדלת ונעל במפתח בנכסי הגר דליכא דמסר ליה, לא הוי חזקה, דאין זה אלא כמבריח ארי מנכסי חבירו. אע"ג דבריש פסחים (דף ד. ושם ד"ה אם) אמר דמשמסר לו מפתח הוי הבית בחזקת שוכר לבדקו, וה"ה לקנותו — ה"מ במוכר ומשכיר לחבירו, דאיכא דמסר ליה דליקני; אבל בנכסי הגר מאן מסר ליה דליקני? ואין נראה לר"י, דבהדיא אמר בפרק הפרה (ב"ק דף נב. ושם ד"ה כיון) דלא קנה במסירת מפתח, ולא מהני מסירת מפתח אלא שלא יצטרך לומר לו: "לך חזק וקני". ודוקא גבי בדיקת חמץ הוא דתלי במסירת מפתח, דמי שמפתח בידו עליו לבדוק, לפי שבידו ליכנס ולבדוק. ומה שפי' נמי דלא קני בנעילת דלת, לא משמע כן בגיטין בהזורק (דף עז: ושם) דקאמר: "תיזיל איהי ותיחוד ותפתח", אלמא בנעילה לחודה קניא, שלא היתה יכולה לעשות מנעול דבשבת היה. ואפי' דאסור לקנות בשבת, בשכ"מ שרי, שלא תטרף דעתו עליו, כדאמר לקמן. ולא דמי נעילת דלת למבריח ארי, דדוקא נתן צרור דסכר מינה מיא הוא דאמר בסמוך דהוי מבריח ארי; אבל הכא שנועל בפני כל אדם ואין מניח אדם ליכנס, מוכח מילתא שהבית הוא שלו, וקני בנעילה לחוד. וכן מוכח לקמן (בבא בתרא דף נז.) גבי הא דתנן: "אלו דברים שיש להן חזקה ואלו דברים שאין להם חזקה", ופריך בגמ': "מ"ש רישא ומ"ש סיפא?" אמר עולא: כל שאילו בנכסי הגר לא קנה כו'. וקתני סיפא: "הכניס תרנגולין בתוך הבית ה"ז חזקה", וקנה נמי בנכסי הגר. וה"ט דהתם דקנה — משום דמסתמא כשנתן שם תרנגולין נעל דלת לשמרן, אלמא דקנה בנעילה. אבל קשה לרשב"א, דאמר לקמן: "הבונה פלטרין בנכסי הגר ובא אחר והעמיד להן דלתות — קנה", והתם מיירי בנעל, דאי לא נעל אמאי קנה? הא לבני בעלמא הוא דאפיך כמו קמא, שכל אדם יכול ליכנס כשלא נעל. אלא ודאי בנעל איירי, ומשמע דוקא שהעמיד דלתות, אבל לא העמיד דלתות — לא קנה בנעילה:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 52b:10:1.english: "If he locked or fenced [the property], even a minimal amount," etc. - In the Gemara, Rashi explains that this "locked" means that he fixed a lock onto the door, which is [an act of] building. But if he merely closed the door and locked it with a key, in the property of a convert, where there is no one who handed it over to him, it is not a [valid] chazakah, for this is no different from driving away a lion from his fellow's property. Although at the beginning of Pesachim (4a, s.v. "Im") it says that once [the owner] has handed him the key, the house is presumed to be in the possession of the renter for purposes of searching it [for chametz], and the same applies to acquiring it — that applies only to a seller or a lessor to his fellow, where there is someone who handed it over to him so that he would acquire it; but in the property of a convert, who handed it over to him so that he would acquire it? But this does not seem right to Rabbeinu Yitzchak, for [the Gemara] said explicitly in the chapter of Haparah (Bava Kamma 52a, s.v. "Kevan") that one does not acquire by handing over a key, and handing over a key is effective only so that he need not say to him: "Go, take possession and acquire." And it is specifically with regard to the search for chametz that [the law] depends on the handing over of a key, because one who has the key in his hand is responsible to search, since it is in his hand to enter and search. Also, as for what [Rashi] explained, that one does not acquire by locking a door — this does not appear to be the case in Gittin, in the chapter Hazorek (77b, there), where it says: "Let her go and be alone [with him] and open [the door]," which shows that by locking alone one acquires, [for the reason that] she could not have made a lock because it was Shabbat. And even though it is forbidden to acquire on Shabbat, for a person on his deathbed it is permitted, so that his mind will not be disturbed over it, as [the Gemara] says later. And locking a door is not comparable to driving away a lion; for it is only [in the case of] one who placed a stone [pebble] that blocks water from it that [the Gemara] said shortly afterward that it is [like] driving away a lion. But here, where he locks in the face of every person and does not allow anyone to enter, it is evident that the house is his, and he acquires by locking alone. And so it is also evident later (Bava Batra 57a), with regard to that which we learned in the Mishnah: "These are the things that have a chazakah, and these are the things that do not have a chazakah," and the Gemara asks: "What is the difference between the first clause and the last clause?" Ulla said: Anything that, if it were done in the property of a convert, he would not acquire, etc. And the last clause teaches: "If he brought chickens into the house, this is a chazakah," and he acquires in the property of a convert as well. And the reason there that he acquires is that presumably, when he placed the chickens there, he locked the door to guard them; evidently he acquired by locking. But this is difficult for the Rashba, who says later: "One who builds palaces on the property of a convert, and another comes and sets up doors for them — he acquires." And there it is speaking of a case where he locked, for if he did not lock, why would he acquire? It is merely building that he reversed, like the first one, since anyone can enter when he has not locked. Rather, it must certainly be speaking of a case where he locked, and it implies that [this is] specifically when he set up doors, but if he did not set up doors, he does not acquire by locking.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 52b:10:2.hebrew: נעל וגדר ופרץ כל שהוא - פ"ה דל"ג "בפניו", משום דבנכסי הגר לא שייך "לפניו". ואינה קשיא, דאיכא למימר משום דנותן מתנה ואחין שחלקו נקט "בפניו". ומיהו ל"ג ליה, דדייק בגמ' אברייתא דרב שרביא: "בפניו — אין, שלא בפניו — לא", ואמתני' ה"ל למידק. ועוד, דבעי רב במתנה, היאך תפשוט ממתני' דאנותן מתנה קתני "בפניו" אי גרס לה:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 52b:10:2.english: "He locked, fenced, or breached [the property] even a little" - Rashi (Peirush HaKuntres) holds that the text does not read "in his presence," since regarding the property of a convert, "in his presence" does not apply. And this is not difficult, for one could say that [the Mishnah] stated "in his presence" because of [the cases of] one who gives a gift and brothers who divided [an inheritance]. However, we do not omit it, because the Gemara draws an inference from the baraita of Rav Sheravya: "In his presence, yes; not in his presence, no," and it should have drawn the inference from the Mishnah. Furthermore, Rav raised a question about [the case of] a gift; how could you resolve it from the Mishnah, since regarding one who gives a gift it states "in his presence," if one reads it [that way]?

Tosafot on Bava Batra 52b:1:1.hebrew: דברים העשוין להשאיל ולהשכיר ואמר לקוחים הן בידי אינו נאמן - וקשה, דאמר בפ' כל הנשבעין (שבועות דף מו. ושם): א"ר יהודה: ראוהו שהטמין כלים תחת כנפיו ויצא, ואמר "לקוחין הן בידי" — אין נאמן. ולא אמרן אלא בבעל הבית שאינו עשוי למכור כליו, ולא אמרן אלא בדברים שאין עשוין להטמין, ולא אמרן אלא בדברי' העשוין להשאיל ולהשכיר. אלמא דאפילו בדברים העשוין להשאיל ולהשכיר נאמן אי ליכא כל הני מילי דקאמר: שאין עשוי למכור כליו, וכלים שאין דרכן להטמין. ונראה לר"ת דגרס התם: ובכולהו נמי כי ליתנהו, לא אמרן אלא בדברים שאין עשוין להשאיל ולהשכיר; אבל דברים העשוין להשאיל ולהשכיר, אפי' ליתנהו לחד מהני — אין נאמן. וכן גורס רב האי בשערים (שער מ), וכן ר"ח, וכן מוכח בשילהי המקבל (ב"מ דף קטז.). וא"ת: דתנא בהגוזל בתרא (ב"ק דף קיד:): המכיר כליו וספריו ביד אחר ויצא שם גנבה בעיר — ישבע כמה הוציא ויטול. והשתא, אפי' לא יצא שם גנבה יהא נאמן לומר שגנבוה, מיגו דאי בעי אמר "השאלתי לך"; דספרים הן עשוין להשאיל, דאפי' ספרא דאגדתא אמר הכא דעשוין להשאיל, כ"ש שאר ספרים, כדאמר בנערה שנתפתתה (כתובות דף נ.): "וצדקתו עומדת לעד" — זה הכותב ספרים ומשאילן לאחרים. ואין לומר דלא מהימן במיגו לומר דגנובים, משום דאחזוקי אינשי בגנבי לא מחזקינן, כדאמר בכל הנשבעין (שבועות דף מו:). דלא דמי: דהתם ודאי אינו נאמן לאחזוקי ההוא גברא בגנבי אפי' במיגו, אבל הכא שאינו אומר "פלוני גנבם" אלא שהם גנובים — מהימן שפיר, דכמה גנבים יש בעולם. ואין לומר נמי דלאו מיגו הוא, שאינו טוען ברצון "השאלתי לך", לפי שאותו יודע בו שהוא משקר; דהא לעיל (בבא בתרא דף לא.) אמר דנאמן לומר "של אבותי הוא, שלקחוה מאבותיך", במיגו דאי בעי אמר "מינך זבינתיה", אע"פ שהוא יודע דלאו מיניה זבנה. וכן בפרק שני דכתובות (דף טו: וע"ש בתוס' ד"ה ומודה) תנן דנאמן לומר "שדה זו של אביך היתה ולקחתיה הימנו", במיגו דאי בעי אמר "לא היתה של אביך מעולם", אע"פ שהבן יודע שהיתה של אביו. ומהנהו עזי דאכלי חושלי בנהרדעא לעיל (בבא בתרא דף לו.) — אין ראיה, דאיכא למימר כגון שמכחישו ואומר שלא אכלו כל כך, דהשתא הוי מיגו טוב. ותירץ ר"ת דהתם מיירי באדם שאין עשוין להשאיל ולהשכיר לזה שקנאם, כגון דלא גייס ביה. ולפי זה, אם עשוי להשאיל לו, אפי' לא יצא לו שם גנבה נאמן לומר שהם גנובים במיגו. ולמה"ר דודי נראה דלא מהימן במיגו, דהוי מיגו להוציא, אע"פ שנוטל דמים שהוציא:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 52b:1:1.english: "Items that are made to be lent and rented, and he said, 'They were purchased by me' — he is not believed" - This is difficult, for it says in the chapter Kol HaNishba'in (Shevuot 46a, there): Rav Yehuda said: If they saw him hide vessels under his cloak and go out, and he said, "They were purchased by me" — he is not believed. And we said this only regarding a householder, who is not apt to sell his vessels; and we said this only regarding items that are not usually hidden; and we said this only regarding items that are made to be lent and rented. Evidently, even regarding items made to be lent and rented, he is believed if not all of these conditions that [Rav Yehuda] stated are present: that he is not apt to sell his vessels, and that these are vessels that are not usually hidden. And it appears to Rabbeinu Tam that the text there reads: "And in all of them too, when they are absent, we said this only regarding items that are not made to be lent and rented; but items that are made to be lent and rented, even if one of these [conditions] is absent — he is not believed." And so Rav Hai reads in [his work] Sha'arim (Gate 40), and so [does] Rabbeinu Chananel, and so it is proven at the end of [the chapter] HaMekabel (Bava Metzia 116a). And if you say: For it was taught in the last chapter of HaGozel (Bava Kamma 114b): One who recognizes his vessels and his books in the hand of another, and a reputation of theft had gone out in the city — [the buyer] swears how much he paid and [the owner] takes [the items]. Now, even if no reputation of theft had gone out, he should be believed to say that they were stolen, by virtue of a migo, [namely] that if he wished, he could say, "I lent them to you"; for books are made to be lent, since even a book of aggadah the Gemara said here is made to be lent, all the more so other books, as stated in [the chapter] Na'arah SheNitpateta (Ketubot 50a): "And his righteousness endures forever" — this is one who writes books and lends them to others. And one cannot say that he is not believed with a migo to say that they were stolen, because we do not make people into presumed thieves, as stated in Kol HaNishba'in (Shevuot 46b). For it is not comparable: there, he is certainly not believed to cast that man as a thief even with a migo, but here, where he does not say "So-and-so stole them" but only that they were stolen — he is properly believed, for there are many thieves in the world. Nor can one say that it is not a migo, since he does not willingly claim "I lent them to you," because that [claimant] knows that he is lying; for above (Bava Batra 31a) it says that he is believed to say, "It belonged to my ancestors, who bought it from your ancestors," by virtue of a migo that if he wished he could say, "I bought it from you," even though he knows that he did not buy it from him. And so too in the second chapter of Ketubot (15b; see there in Tosafot, s.v. U'Modeh) we learned that he is believed to say, "This field was your father's and I bought it from him," by virtue of a migo that if he wished he could say, "It was never your father's," even though the son knows that it was his father's. And as for those goats that ate the shoots (chushlei) in Neharde'a above (Bava Batra 36a) — there is no proof, for one can say [that case is] where he denies him and says that they did not eat so much, so that now it is a good migo. And Rabbeinu Tam answered that there [in Bava Kamma] it speaks of a person from whom such items are not made to be lent and rented to this one who bought them, for example, where he is not on friendly terms with him. And according to this, if he is one who is accustomed to lend to him, even if no reputation of theft had gone out, [the buyer] is believed to say that they were stolen, by virtue of a migo. But to my teacher, R. David, it appears that he is not believed with a migo, since it is a migo to extract [property from another], even though [the buyer] takes the money that he paid.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 52b:2:1.hebrew: אימא מעיסתו קימץ - אע"ג דלא טעין הכי, אלא אומר: "מבית אבי אמא" — מ"מ נאמן, במיגו דאי בעי אמר: "מעיסתי קמצתי":
Tosafot on Bava Batra 52b:2:1.english: Say that he took a handful from his [own] dough - Even though he does not claim this, but rather says, "[It came] from my mother's father's house," nevertheless he is believed, by virtue of a migo: for if he wanted, he could have said, "I took a handful from my own dough."

Tosafot on Bava Batra 52b:6:1.hebrew: דטרחא קמי יתמי אימא לא גזלה מיתמי - קשה לרשב"א: דאדרבה, מהאי טעמא דטרחא קמי יתמי גזלה מיתמי, כדאמר בהשולח (גיטין דף לה.): בההוא הנאה דטרחא קמי יתמי אתיא לאורויי. ותירץ: דה"נ קאמר הכא: קמ"ל דלא אמרינן דלא גזלה, אלא אדרבה אתיא לאורויי, כדאמר בגיטין:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 52b:6:1.english: "Since she toils on behalf of the orphans, I might say she did not take it by force from the orphans" - This is difficult for the Rashba: On the contrary, for this very reason, that she toils on behalf of the orphans, she has taken [the property] by force from the orphans, as stated in [the chapter] HaShole'ach (Gittin 35a): "For that benefit of toiling on behalf of the orphans, she comes to rule [for herself]." And he answered: That here too, [the Gemara] is saying this: It teaches us that we do not say that she did not take it by force; rather, on the contrary, she comes to rule [for herself], as stated in Gittin:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 52b:7:1.hebrew: אטו כל הני לאו בני חזקה נינהו - פירוש: דמשמע ליה "בד"א" — במחזיק הוא דבעי ג"ש חזקה, כלומר: במידי דשייך חזקה; אבל בנותן כו'. מש"ה פריך: אטו הני, כגון נותן מתנה והאחין שחלקו, לאו בני חזקת ג"ש נינהו?
Tosafot on Bava Batra 52b:7:1.english: Is it that all of these are not subject to chazakah? - Explanation: It understood "In what case is this said?" [to mean] that it is only with one who holds [the property] that three years of chazakah are required — that is, in a matter to which chazakah applies; but with one who gives, etc. [no such requirement applies]. Therefore [the Gemara] asks: Is it that these — such as one who gives a gift and brothers who divided [an inheritance] — are not subject to a three-year chazakah?
